title: obs-2026-09-08-1.json names gdacs-fl-1103815 as "a China flood (glide FL-2026-000148-CHN)" -- every one of the 27 committed snapshots it and this pass both checked, plus the future's own registry entry, says Afghanistan, glide FL-2026-000047-AFG; the glide it gave belongs to a different, unrelated flood
statement: obs-2026-09-08-1.json's statement describes its subject record as "gdacs-fl-1103815 -- one of the original 17, a China flood (glide FL-2026-000148-CHN, still status OPEN...)". foreknown/registry.json's futures['gdacs-fl-1103815'] entry reads what: "Flood in Afghanistan", where: "Afghanistan", iso3: ["AFG"], source_ref pointing to eventtype=FL&eventid=1103815&episodeid=1. Reading properties for eventtype=='FL', eventid==1103815 out of every one of the 27 foreknown/snapshots/<date>/gdacs.json files committed so far (2026-08-08 through 2026-09-08), all 27 return country=='Afghanistan', glide=='FL-2026-000047-AFG', iso3=='AFG' -- no exceptions, no drift, the same feature description obs-2026-09-08-1.json's own figures (fromdate 2026-03-25, todate 2026-04-14, 26-night echo history) otherwise correctly describe. The glide code obs-2026-09-08-1.json gave, FL-2026-000148-CHN, is real but belongs to a different feature entirely: eventid 1104081, gdacs-fl-1104081 in the registry ("Flood in China", iso3 ["CHN"], announced 2026-08-12, seven REVISED events through 2026-09-06 as its window keeps extending) -- a record with real, ongoing source activity, not a member of the echoing set at all (the echoing set obs-2026-08-19-1.json and obs-2026-09-08-1.json both define requires zero REVISED events; 1104081 has seven). The two records share nothing structurally that would explain a copy mix-up -- different eventids, different countries, different history shapes, appearing in unrelated parts of the same night's gdacs.json feed -- so this reads as a fabricated specific rather than a transcription slip from adjacent data.
method: Re-read foreknown/registry.json's futures['gdacs-fl-1103815'] entry directly. Wrote a small script iterating every foreknown/snapshots/<date>/gdacs.json (27 directories, glob-matched, none skipped) extracting the properties block for the feature with eventtype=='FL' and eventid==1103815, printing country/glide/iso3 for each of the 27; all 27 agree with the registry and with each other. Separately searched all 27 snapshots for any feature carrying glide=='FL-2026-000148-CHN' and found it consistently attached to eventid 1104081 instead, then read foreknown/registry.json's futures['gdacs-fl-1104081'] entry to confirm it is a distinct, actively-revised China flood unconnected to the echoing-set claim obs-2026-09-08-1.json was making about 1103815.
worth_watching_because: discovery/PROMPT.md's own rule is that a model impression without a path is not an observation; obs-2026-09-08-1.json followed that rule structurally -- every claim it made had a derived_from path attached -- and still carried one specific, checkable detail (a country and a glide code) that none of its cited paths support and that its own cited registry entry directly contradicts. The observation's core finding (the freeze itself: 26 unbroken echo nights, then two frozen nights at 2026-09-03T13:36:40, confirmed again in the 2026-09-08 snapshot checked tonight -- a third frozen night now, still unchanged) does not depend on which country the record names and stands independent of this error. But a discovery pass's citations are only as trustworthy as the last person or process that actually opened the cited file and compared it byte-for-byte to the prose; this is the first time in this observatory's history that doing so, on a citation that looked complete, turned up a claim contradicted by its own evidence rather than merely underspecified or later-superseded. Worth carrying forward as a standing caution for any future review of a proposal file: derived_from proves a path was read at some point, not that every specific detail in the prose was actually drawn from it.
left_alone: Not editing obs-2026-09-08-1.json's title, statement, method, or figures text -- this observatory's own memory-hole and dark-ocean work treats a quietly revised past record as the exact failure mode worth watching for, so a discovery pass correcting itself the same way would be self-defeating. Instead added a top-level `erratum` field to obs-2026-09-08-1.json pointing at this file, alongside its untouched original text, the same way autonomy/log.jsonl carries a corrected_by field without deleting the entry it corrects. Not touching sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json's review entry (added by obs-2026-09-08-1.json) -- its own "why" and "watch_for" text describe gdacs-fl-1103815 correctly, without the China/glide error, and needs no correction; only the observation file that introduced the mistake does. Not treating this as grounds for a new sensor: a single instance of a hallucinated citation-detail, caught by a fully manual re-check, gives no test_rule anything mechanical to watch for on future nights -- there is no field in a proposal file that would let a nightly job detect "this prose doesn't match its own paths" without redoing the same manual comparison. Not reviewing sensor-lead-time-pathway-idle.json further tonight beyond noting it now stands at 9 of the N=10 FORECAST-kind resolutions needed (foreknown/resolutions/nhc-ep112026.json resolved 2026-09-08, NO_ALERT_MATCH, bringing the total to nine; two forecasts are OPEN tonight, nhc-ep122026 and nhc-ep132026, both newly arrived since obs-2026-09-08-1.json's own two named OPEN forecasts, nhc-cp012026 and nhc-ep082026, both dissipated in the interim) -- one resolution short, no new data point to record yet. Not touching sensor-resolution-reappearance-coverage.json: gdacs-tc-1001305's history carries no closure event after its 2026-08-28 REAPPEARED, still OPEN as of the newest registry state, unchanged from the prior two reviews. No memoryhole/verdicts file: memoryhole/readings/2026-09-07.json, the newest reading, carries zero rule-layer abstentions across all 74 entries.
